title: Evaluation of changing pigmented lesions
text: A changing pigmented lesion with concerning morphology should receive clinician assessment; dermoscopy and biopsy may be considered according to the clinical context. Evolution over time is an important feature to document.

title: Persistent scaly lesions on sun-exposed skin
text: Persistent scaly lesions on chronically sun-exposed skin merit clinical examination because benign inflammatory conditions and keratinocytic neoplasia can overlap in appearance. Management depends on examination findings and diagnostic certainty.

title: Inflammatory dermatoses and remote assessment
text: Remote assessment of inflammatory dermatoses can support history-taking and follow-up, but morphology, distribution, treatment response, and red flags should be interpreted in clinical context. Diagnostic uncertainty should be stated explicitly.

title: Limits of remote lesion assessment
text: When image quality, lighting, scale, palpation findings, or lesion evolution cannot be adequately assessed remotely, the system should communicate uncertainty and recommend appropriate in-person assessment rather than overstate diagnostic confidence.

title: Safety escalation for severe mucocutaneous presentations
text: Blistering eruptions associated with systemic symptoms or significant mucosal involvement can represent serious disease and require prompt clinical assessment. Remote text generation should not delay urgent evaluation when red flags are present.
